newsitem.title: USA: Apple Q4 cash rises to $1.7 billion.
newsitem.headline: Apple Q4 cash rises to $1.7 billion.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc said its cash and short term investments totaled more than $1.7 billion in the fourth quarter ended in September, up from $952 million in the year-ago quarter.
Total cash totaled $1.4 billion at the end of the third fiscal quarter.
The company earlier reported a $0.20 per share profit in the fourth quarter, which compared with a First Call consensus estimate for a $0.30 per share loss.
In announcing the earnings, it also said unit shipments for the quarter fell about 26 pct from the year-ago fourth quarter to about 932,000, but were up 11 percent from the third quarter.
It also said its gross margins rose to 22 percent from 18.5 percent the year before.

"We continue to make progress in strengthening Apple's financial condition, as our $410 million in positive cash flow from operations during the quarter suggests," executive vice president and chief financial officer Fred Anderson said in a statement.

"We've reduced inventories by nearly $400 million since June and completed the quarter with over $1.7 billion in cash and short-term investments. Gross margins increased due to several factors, including declining component costs, improved manufacturing efficiencies, and sales of previously reserved inventory," he said.
